expectations.text: Includes a dedicated, sourced section addressing title status / titled land vs Rights of Possession risk specific to Boquete
expectations.evidence: output.md has a standalone `## Is Boquete titled?` section (lines 18-24) that cites the Panamanian constitution (Título X, Arts. 286 and 291) for the 10km border-zone rule, names ANATI and the Registro Público, explains derecho posesorio (Rights of Possession) vs. titled finca land specific to Bajo Boquete formal developments vs. agricultural/hillside land outside town, cites TheLatinvestor for the foreign-buyer-regret pattern, and links to an internal titled-vs-ROP guide. The claim is also reinforced in two FAQ entries ('Is land in Boquete titled or Rights of Possession?' and 'Can foreigners even buy property this close to the Costa Rica border?').

expectations.text: Includes at least one concrete cost-of-living or cost-to-buy figure with a named source
expectations.evidence: `## What it costs to live in Boquete` section gives multiple named-source figures, e.g. 'a one-bedroom apartment near the town center runs roughly $650-$800/month... (International Living; Wise cost-of-living, checked July 2026)' and 'roughly $58/month for electricity, water, and garbage on an 85 m2 apartment... (Wise, checked July 2026)'.

expectations.text: Includes an explicit 'who this suits / who it doesn't' section naming a type of buyer it is NOT good for
expectations.evidence: `## Who Boquete suits - and who it doesn't` section explicitly lists six buyer types it doesn't suit: beach-lifestyle seekers, anyone needing hospital-level care nearby, investors chasing liquidity/yield, anyone allergic to rain (landslide/break-in risk cited), anyone relying on grid power without backup, and buyers who want to walk everywhere without a car.

expectations.text: Includes practical access information (distance/time to nearest airport, road quality, whether a car is required)
expectations.evidence: `## Getting there and getting around` section: 'Fly into David's Enrique Malek International Airport (DAV)... about 40 minutes / 26-30 miles to Boquete on a paved, four-lane road'; and on car necessity: 'Once you're outside downtown, a car stops being optional - the roads climbing into Alto Boquete, Jaramillo, and the hillside communities generally don't have sidewalks.' Also echoed in FAQ ('How far is Boquete from an airport?' and 'Do I need a car in Boquete?').

The `## FAQ` section contains 5 questions: AC/heating need, titled vs. ROP land, foreign ownership near the border, distance to nearest airport, and need for a car / internet reliability for remote work.

expectations.text: The page does not spend more than a sentence or two on scenery/atmosphere description disconnected from a purchase question (avoids travel-writing drift)
expectations.evidence: Climate/elevation descriptions in Identity and Positioning are consistently tied back to a buying-relevant point (AC/heating cost, elevation affecting property value/comfort) rather than standalone scenery prose. No passages describe views, ambiance, or landscape purely for atmosphere; the closest is the single 'eternal spring' framing in Positioning, which is immediately used to set up the AC/heating differentiator rather than lingering on description.

claims.evidence: Output shows the two disagreeing source ranges (International Living $1,403-$2,600 vs. other aggregations $2,500-$3,500) and explicitly states INEC does not publish a Boquete-specific index, rather than presenting a single cherry-picked number. This matches the transcript's stated approach in Section 5.

suggestions.assertion: The page does not spend more than a sentence or two on scenery/atmosphere description disconnected from a purchase question (avoids travel-writing drift)
suggestions.reason: This assertion is somewhat subjective and hard to fail cleanly for a page like this — the skill's own house voice (inline-sourced, drawback-oriented, Investopedia-style) makes travel-writing drift unlikely by construction. Consider tightening it to something more discriminating, e.g. 'no paragraph exceeds N words without a sourced fact or purchase-relevant claim,' so it would actually catch a regression rather than passing by default whenever the skill is followed at all.

output.md contains one overstated sourcing claim not caught by any expectation: the sentence 'Multiple sources researching foreign-buyer regret in Panama name exactly this pattern... as one of the most frequently cited mistakes' cites only a single named source (TheLatinvestor) in both the inline citation and the numbered Sources list. Given the skill's stated discipline of sourcing every figure precisely, a spot-check assertion like 'every claim of consensus ("multiple sources," "commonly cited") is backed by more than one named source in the Sources list' would catch this class of quiet overstatement.

eval_feedback.overall: All 6 expectations pass with genuine, non-superficial evidence — this is a strong output that follows the skill's sourcing and structure requirements closely, including flagging its own unverifiable claims (border-zone cadastral boundary, finca-level title status, post-2010 census figure) rather than guessing. The two suggestions above are minor: one about assertion discriminability, one about a specific overstated 'multiple sources' claim that slipped past sourcing discipline.
